name: Berkeley collaboration’s self-aligned double-gate FinFET
description: A UC Berkeley-led collaboration demonstrated a MOS transistor with a short, thin silicon fin, self-aligned side gates, and raised source and drain. Gate control from both sides helped suppress short-channel effects. The collaboration reported the initial device as a folded-channel MOSFET and later reported a p-channel FinFET.

links.statement: The collaboration built its demonstrated double-gate FinFET on the DELTA structure, reducing the height of the fin to make the device using a quasi-planar process.
links.scope: Device design and fabrication of the Berkeley collaboration’s prototype.
links.alternatives: Hu recalled independently sketching a fin-shaped concept during the initial proposal. Hisamoto joined the project shortly after that proposal and contributed to building the devices.

evidence.locator: Printed p. 1032, structure, measurements and reference [1]; p. 1033, Fig. 1
evidence.supports: The research report describes the shortened fin, aligned side gates and elevated source and drain, and includes measurements from fabricated devices.

evidence.locator: Printed p. 2320, Introduction and Device Fabrication
evidence.supports: The project authors explicitly identify DELTA as the design basis and describe the reduction in vertical feature height for quasi-planar fabrication.

Independent interviews corroborate that DELTA developer Hisamoto joined on leave from Hitachi and worked on the concept and fabrication. The authors also record Hu’s account of a separately sketched fin concept.

date.basis: The 1998 IEDM proceedings contain the prototype measurements.

events.statement: The collaboration reported measurements from its folded-channel silicon transistor at IEDM.

date.basis: The 1999 IEDM proceedings report the fabricated p-channel devices.

events.statement: The collaboration reported p-channel FinFETs with measured devices down to 18 nm gate length.

evidence.supports: The report separates fabricated p-channel devices from simulated scaling.

earliest_record.rationale: The 1998 proceedings paper records the already fabricated folded-channel prototype. The 1999 report documents the p-channel adaptation.

unresolved.note: The interviews differ on who first proposed the fin geometry for the project. The design link concerns the demonstrated device.
The sources here leave open which Berkeley process steps or design choices transferred to specific production foundry processes.
